newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open weaker, eye on 10-yr auctions.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open weaker, eye on 10-yr auctions.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker in moderate trade on Wednesday, with investors focused on the outcome of both Canadian and U.S. 10-year bond auctions being held today.

"As of Friday the market started to correct and it's become a buyers' market, and the worst thing in a buyers' market is supply," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn Capital Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.39 to C$119.70 to yield 6.495 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 2/32 to yield 6.50 percent. The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to one basis point from two basis points at Monday's close.
Both Canadian and U.S. investors are awaiting the results of the 10-year auctions which will be released early this afternoon.
In Canada, the federal government will auction C$2.3 billion of bonds with an unspecified coupon due June 1, 2008. Results of the auction will be released at 1315 EDT/1715 GMT.
The U.S. Treasury will auction US$12 billion of 10-year notes with results expected at 1330 EDT/1730 GMT.

While the weakness that has infected fixed-income markets since Friday's sharp selloff should help make the new issues more attractive, analysts said there was no guarantee the auctions would be well bid.
"We're not sure if the buyers will like these prices yet. The buyers are in no hurry to step into the market," said Dong. "You're probably going to see weakness over the next few sessions."
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.15 to C$109.28 to yield 5.972 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 2/32 to yield 6.23 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 26 basis points from 29 basis points at Tuesday's close.
